attempts.label: DANDI:000931
attempts.paper_title: A mechanosensory feedback that uncouples external and self-generated sensory responses in the olfactory cortex
attempts.entry_title: Sniffing and odor responses in the olfactory cortex (Dehaqani, Michelon et al. 2024)
attempts.summary: None of the paper's main findings could be tested, because the dandiset holds one mouse out of 22 and none of the breathing, odor-trial, brain-area or waveform data the analyses need. That covers the sorting of inhalations into slow and fast, the sniff-driven changes in piriform odor responses, the model of speed and concentration inputs, the airflow tuning, the bulbectomy effects and the sniff-invariant concentration code. All 37 claims are blocked, and the paper says its processed data are available on request. The file holds only spike times for 1013 units, with no brain area to select piriform neurons. The checks that could be made agree with the paper: unit quality measures match the reported ranges, and units near the probe tip show a 2.78 Hz rhythm within the mouse breathing range.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Dehaqani, Michelon, Patella, Petrucco, Piasini and Iurilli (2024) on dandiset 000931. The dandiset holds one NWB file, the sorted spike times of 1013 units from one mouse, placed in the concentration-series experiment only by a keyword, with no breathing signal, inhalation times, odor trials, airflow pulses, unit waveforms or brain regions. Every claim of the paper needs at least one of these, so all are blocked; the notebook lists what the file holds and checks the unit table against its description and the paper's spike-sorting criteria.

outcomes.statement: Inhalation durations appear bimodal, and a Gaussian-mixture and hierarchical clustering of inhalation waveforms sorts them into slow and fast inhalations; fast inhalations are shorter and have steeper airflow changes than slow ones.

outcomes.quote: Since the distribution of inhalation durations appeared bimodal, we developed a semi-unsupervised method that sorted inhalations into slow and fast depending on their airflow rate waveforms ... Fast inhalations had shorter duration and steeper changes in airflow rate than slow inhalations.
outcomes.notes: The dandiset's one file holds spike times of one mouse and none of the nasal airflow signal or inhalation times, which the criterion needs; it also pools the eight awake mice of the leave-one-mouse-out test, which are not in the dandiset. The paper says its processed data are available on request, and no public source holds them.

outcomes.statement: Classifiers cannot decode the experimental condition from the spike waveform features of the recorded units, suggesting homogeneous sampling of cell types across conditions.
outcomes.source: Results, Sniffing causes unstable odor responses in the PCx, paragraph 2; Figures S6G and S6H
outcomes.quote: The distributions of the waveform features were comparable across experiments, and neither crossvalidated linear nor non-linear classifiers could discriminate an experimental condition based on the spike waveforms of the units recorded (see STAR Methods).
outcomes.notes: The dandiset's one file holds spike times of one mouse and none of unit waveforms, which the criterion needs; it also pools the recordings of the other experimental conditions, which are not in the dandiset. The paper says its processed data are available on request, and no public source holds them.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds one NWB file from one of the paper's 22 mice, with the spike times of 1013 sorted units and their labels. The four signals the Methods say were recorded besides the spikes (the nasal airflow, the odor signal of the photo-ionization detector, the odor-trial TTL and the inhalation-onset TTL), the artificial airflow pulses, the unit waveforms and the brain area of each unit are not in it, and neither are the other 21 mice. All 37 claims need some of these, so none can be tested. The paper says its processed data are available from the lead contact on request, and its code deposit (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10381293) loads preprocessed files it does not hold.

The file gives no brain area for its units and has no electrodes table. Phy-good units lie along the whole probe (depth 80 to 3840 for the 359 good units, with 97, 127, 53 and 82 of them in the four 1000-um bands), so they include structures above the piriform cortex, and the paper's selection of PCx layer 2 and 3 units cannot be repeated. The experiment the mouse belongs to is given only by the keyword "Concentration Series", and the odors given are not stated.

KSLabel is "good" for all 1013 units and ContamPct is 100 for all of them. Kilosort labels a cluster good when its estimated contamination is low, so the two columns contradict each other and say nothing about the units. The Phy curation (quality) is good for 359 units, mua for 10 and missing for 644.

Of the unit table's columns only quality, spike_times and unit_name have a description. The others (KSLabel, sh, ch, depth, Amplitude, amp, ContamPct, fr, n_spikes, original_cluster_id) say "No description.", and depth, Amplitude and amp have no unit. The session description is the converter's default.

The file's related_publications names the bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2023.04.04.535405), not the published paper, and the two 2024 versions of the dandiset (0.240305.0939 and 0.240305.0945) do not name the paper; version 0.261011.1559 and the draft do. All versions hold the same asset.

What could be checked is consistent with the paper. The Phy-good units have ISI violation rates (median 0.0066, Q1 0, Q3 0.029, by the Hill et al. formula at 1.5 ms) and presence ratios (1 in every quartile) in the ranges the Methods report, all fire above the 0.5 Hz threshold, no unit is duplicated, and the summed activity of the good units nearest the probe tip (by the standard Neuropixels 1.0 channel map, which depth follows; the file names no probe) peaks at 2.78 Hz, within the range of mouse breathing; the check of the half frequency leaves that peak at 2.78 Hz.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier queried the archive API and tested helper functions on synthetic inputs. It gave its own outcome for each claim; all 37 agree with the record. Its points that concern no single claim were answered as follows. B3, the claims file path is outside the bundle - the cell now prints the 37 claim ids of mechano.CLAIM_NEEDS and runs the comparison only where the claims file is present. B4, the spectral argmax can report a harmonic - mechano.spectral_peak now moves the peak to its subharmonic when the power there is at least half the peak, shown on synthetic 3 Hz trains (largest power 6.01 Hz, checked peak 2.98 Hz); the 0 to 1000 band stays at 2.78 Hz, and the 2000 to 3000 band moves from 2.93 to 1.51 Hz. The depth convention is now checked against the data - depth lies within 20 of 20 + 20 floor(ch / 2), the standard Neuropixels 1.0 map with channel 0 at the tip, and the notebook says the probe type is assumed, as the file names none.

entries.name: dehaqani-2024
entries.title: Sniffing and odor responses in the olfactory cortex (Dehaqani, Michelon et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Dehaqani, Michelon, Patella, Petrucco, Piasini and Iurilli (2024) on dandiset 000931. The dandiset holds one NWB file, the sorted spike times of 1013 units from one mouse, placed in the concentration-series experiment only by a keyword, with no breathing signal, inhalation times, odor trials, airflow pulses, unit waveforms or brain regions. Every claim of the paper needs at least one of these, so all are blocked; the notebook lists what the file holds and checks the unit table against its description and the paper's spike-sorting criteria.
